Yesterday's PARTIAL classification driven by Shimla-EN's 404 fallback regression has cleared — Shimla-EN renders 466 KB with 36/55/14 h2/h3/h4 and a clean 'Shimla' h1.

regression_matrix.evidence: /en/collections lists 102 unique collection links (≥80 bar, +11 vs yesterday). 4 of 4 real-slug probes rendered 200 with content; only the 2 probes I made up returned 404 (expected).

Status held at PARTIAL because the eager-zero pattern reproduces across multiple destinations.

new_defects.title: Hindi destination pages still leak English secondary chrome (alert banner, Save button, top intro banner)
new_defects.evidence: On /hi/destination/jaipur the page body opens with: top banner 'First time visiting India? Safety, scams, what to wear, and more — the honest guide by an Indian family.' (English), the alert card 'Low season for Jaipur / This destination scores 1/5 in the current month...' (English copy from /api/alerts?id=jaipur), and the secondary action button labelled 'Save' (English). Primary copy (h1, title, h2/h3, body) is correctly Hindi.
new_defects.impact: Mixed-language chrome reduces the credibility of the Hindi experience and probably hurts engagement on /hi/. Not a crawl/indexing risk.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app — route the alert message template (server side) and the Save button label (client side) through the i18n message catalog; localise the top intro banner.
new_defects.reproduction: curl -s https://www.nakshiq.com/hi/destination/jaipur | grep -oE 'Low season for [A-Za-z]+' returns the English string. /api/alerts?id=jaipur (no locale param) always returns English copy.

new_defects.title: Hindi explore page mixes Hindi h1/subtitle with English city quick-buttons and English state-name options
new_defects.evidence: /hi/explore body: 'खोजें · 505 गंतव्य · फ़िल्टर करें या मानचित्र देखें' (good) but immediately below: 'START FROM' (label English), 'DELHI / MUMBAI / BANGALORE / CHENNAI / KOLKATA / HYDERABAD' (city buttons English), 'WEEKEND TRIPS →' (English), and the State filter dropdown lists 'Andaman & Nicobar Islands / Lakshadweep / Puducherry / Daman & Diu / Himachal Pradesh / Uttarakhand / Jammu & Kashmir / Ladakh / Rajasthan / ...' all in English.
new_defects.impact: Hindi-locale users see a bilingual page; reduces the feel of the localisation work that has clearly been done elsewhere. Cosmetic.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app — translate the START FROM label, the 6 city quick-button labels, the WEEKEND TRIPS link, and either localise the state names or accept the bilingual convention deliberately.
new_defects.reproduction: Open https://www.nakshiq.com/hi/explore in any browser, see the 'STATE FROM' / 'DELHI' / 'MUMBAI' row immediately below the Hindi subtitle.

new_defects.title: 404 collection slugs return correct status but ship the not-found shell with the homepage <title> instead of a not-found-specific title
new_defects.evidence: GET /en/collections/most-photogenic-india returns HTTP 404 (correct) with a 54,612-byte body. Body contains exactly one NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK marker and the visible 'Lost in the mountains / This trail doesn't exist — yet.' UI (correct). However the <title> is 'NakshIQ — Travel Intelligence for India' (the layout default) rather than something like 'Page not found — NakshIQ'. Same on /en/collections/family-friendly-mountains.
new_defects.impact: Cosmetic only — search crawlers respect the 404 status, so this doesn't risk indexing. But the browser tab title reads 'NakshIQ — Travel Intelligence for India' on a 404 page, which is mildly confusing for users. Minimal effort to fix in the not-found.tsx metadata export.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app — add a metadata export to the relevant not-found.tsx files setting an explicit page title.
new_defects.reproduction: curl -s -o /tmp/x.html -w 'http:%{http_code}' https://www.nakshiq.com/en/collections/most-photogenic-india → http:404; grep -oE '<title>[^<]*</title>' /tmp/x.html → '<title>NakshIQ — Travel Intelligence for India</title>'.

new_defects.title: llms.txt still advertises numeric month sub-routes (/destination/<slug>/<1-12>) but those routes now hard-404
new_defects.evidence: GET /en/destination/jaipur/3 → 404 (was soft-200 fallback yesterday — that part is FIXED). But /llms.txt is still 200 with size 2993 bytes and continues to list the numeric form as a stable contract. So an LLM agent following llms.txt will now hit a hard 404 instead of a soft-200. Status flipped from one kind of broken to another.
new_defects.impact: Low. Bot-friendly contract is technically broken; either the routing should be implemented OR llms.txt should be updated to drop the numeric form. Hard 404 is at least an honest signal; soft-200 was strictly worse.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app + content — pick one of: (a) implement /destination/<slug>/<1-12> as an alias of /destination/<slug>/<month-name>; or (b) update llms.txt and llms-full.txt to drop the numeric form.
new_defects.reproduction: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://www.nakshiq.com/en/destination/jaipur/3 → 404; curl -s https://www.nakshiq.com/llms.txt | grep -E '/destination/.*/[0-9]' returns the numeric examples.

gaps: Itinerary endpoint contract still undocumented — every payload shape I tried returned 'Missing required fields'. A documented schema would let me probe positive paths and validate response bodies.

BUG-007 root cause not determined — confirmed map renders empty across both destination pages and the explore Map view, but did not inspect /api/places (or whichever endpoint the leaflet layer subscribes to) to identify whether the data fetch fails or the layer fails to plot.
